new_or_updated_candidates.mechanism: A recurrent network of explicitly damped oscillatory nodes uses a second history term (AR(2)-equivalent dynamics) with fixed resonance frequencies and trainable cross-frequency recurrent coupling. Golden-ratio-spaced frequencies are tested as a biologically motivated inductive bias.
evidence: MNIST over 10 randomized train/validation realizations: golden RRN 0.759±0.007, LSTM 0.715±0.019, standard RNN 0.617±0.018.
Same-node-count/same-parameter frequency-spacing control: golden RRN 0.759±0.007 vs linear-spaced RRN 0.592±0.004; both 11 nodes and 252 estimable parameters, reported p=4e-14.
Golden vs alternative biologically motivated frequency spacings reported p<1e-14; vs LSTM p=0.0098; vs standard RNN p=1.1e-11.

Synthetic spike-train classification over 1000 realizations: golden RRN 0.635±0.001 vs linear RRN 0.604±0.001, standard RNN 0.575±0.002, LSTM 0.546±0.002; golden RRN higher than other architectures with p<5e-11.

Learned MNIST recurrent weights show stronger low-to-high than high-to-low frequency coupling, t=12.1, p≈1e-25. Spike-train task shows a consistent asymmetry, t=-4.9 under the paper's subtraction convention, p=1.2e-6.
Author repository Mark-Kramer/Resonant-Recurrent-Network publicly provides notebooks for RRN, LSTM, standard-RNN MNIST, and spike-train analyses.
mechanistic_scope: The matched golden-vs-linear 11-node control is the cleanest evidence that frequency placement, not just node count, matters in these tasks.
The paper trains recurrent coupling and readout parameters with standard supervised optimization/backpropagation through time; the learning rule itself is not biologically local.

Absolute MNIST accuracy is modest and the second benchmark is a simple synthetic 100-ms spike-modulation classification task; this is evidence for an inductive bias, not competitive general sequence modeling.

The golden-ratio frequency theory is biologically motivated, but the paper itself states that how simulated oscillator cross-frequency interactions relate to biological neuronal/population mechanisms remains future work.
No clear independent third-party reproduction was located in exact-title/reproduction searches in this run.

new_or_updated_candidates.mechanism: Wave-RNN replaces a dense recurrent transition with circular local convolution initialized as a one-way shift, creating a traveling-wave hidden-state buffer that moves recent inputs instead of overwriting them in place.
evidence: ICLR 2024 paper, official proceedings and OpenReview; official code at akandykeller/Wave_RNNs.
Synthetic addition task: at sequence length T=1000, iRNN test MSE 0.16 and never solved within 60k iterations, while wRNN reached 6e-5 and solved in ~2k iterations in the main table.
Three-random-initialization appendix: T=700 adding MSE iRNN 0.163±2.08e-3 vs wRNN 5.29e-5±3.19e-5; T=1000 iRNN 0.160 vs wRNN 4.36e-5±1.91e-5.
psMNIST main table: wRNN(16c) 96.7% with 47k parameters vs tuned iRNN 92.5% with 68k; sMNIST is a boundary where iRNN is better, 98.5% vs wRNN 97.6%.
Three-seed appendix: psMNIST iRNN 90.85±1.47 vs wRNN 96.60±0.10; noisy sequential CIFAR-10 iRNN 51.80±0.54 vs wRNN 54.70±0.42.
Noisy sequential CIFAR-10 main best-run table: wRNN 55.0% (256 units/435k params) vs iRNN 51.3% (529/336k), but wRNN remains below coRNN 59.0 and LEM 60.5.

Copy-task ablation at T=80: full wRNN ~1e-11 MSE; removing shift initialization degrades to 6e-4, removing both V and shift init to 7e-4; iRNN with shift+V initialization reaches 8e-6, still worse than full wRNN. Authors interpret tied sparse convolution plus shift initialization as critical.
The paper reports substantial hyperparameter sweeps and roughly 1000 GPU-hours for MNIST sweeps, 1600 GPU-hours for noisy sequential CIFAR-10, and 1200 GPU-hours for adding-task sweeps.
mechanistic_scope: This is stronger than analogy because the proposed wave-supporting recurrent structure is directly ablated and transferred to sequence-learning tasks.
The strongest advantage is long-memory/permutation robustness, not universal task dominance: wRNN loses to iRNN on unpermuted sMNIST and to stronger recurrent baselines on noisy sequential CIFAR-10.
Parameter efficiency is task-dependent: wRNN uses fewer parameters than iRNN on psMNIST but more on the reported noisy sequential CIFAR-10 comparison.
Ablations show shift initialization and sparse/tied convolution matter, but they do not prove that biological cortical traveling waves use the same computational mechanism.
Independent third-party reproduction/failure evidence has not yet been established in this clean run.

rejected_or_qualified.lead: Golden-ratio RRN as proof of a biological golden-ratio code
rejected_or_qualified.reason: The AI frequency-spacing ablation is real, but the mapping from this engineered oscillator bank to biological causal mechanism remains unproven and is explicitly left open by the paper.

rejected_or_qualified.lead: Wave-RNN as uniformly superior sequence model
rejected_or_qualified.reason: It excels on long-memory/permuted tasks but loses on plain sMNIST and to coRNN/LEM on noisy sequential CIFAR-10; advantage is scope-specific.
